name: immediate-queryability-reconciliation
body:
Reconciliation for the "graph is immediately queryable" work (human's requirement: root requirement + children + solution-tier reconciliation + global law). Each item authored against the durable nodes; the reviewer resolves.

1. Root and hierarchy [autonomous]. New root `requirements.requirement.graph-immediately-queryable` (feature `graph-consistency`) carries the acceptance scenario verbatim ("add requirement \"foo\" / immediately query and find \"foo\""). It contains the existing `metadata-mutation-graph-consistency` tree (unchanged: no-rescan-for-metadata, planned-node-removal-reflected, projection-delta-atomic, rescan-only-on-code-change, projection-equals-sources) plus the four new children write-through-projection, read-your-writes, read-access-during-session, commit-then-project — one tree. The two old root containments (stakeholder.apg-maintainer → metadata-mutation-graph-consistency, user.suite-agent → metadata-mutation-graph-consistency) were moved UP to graph-immediately-queryable, so there is a single feature root rather than a dangling second tree.

2. Buffer → write-through [with user / coordinator instruction]. `solution.component.derived-projection-buffer` (batched write-back at session end) conflicted with write-through-projection and was REMOVED; replaced by `solution.component.write-through-projection`, which applies each mutation's exact delta synchronously as part of the mutation (durable commit first, then delta). `solution.component.projection-delta-applier` is kept for the exact-delta deletion semantics; the reframed component anchors implemented-by to the real synchronous paths `apg.layers.write_project` and `apg.plan_cmd.write_through`. The old buffer's planned anchors (`apg.session.ProjectionBuffer*`) are now obsolete — those planned nodes and their buffer tasks belong to the plan, which must be revisited.

3. Read-through routing. `solution.component.session-routing` reframed to cover reads, not just writes: `apg query` / suite reads route through the live session (read-through) while it owns db.lbug, or open read-only on the direct path. Anchored implemented-by to real `apg.cmd_query` (the read path to reshape) plus the existing planned `apg.session.Coordinator.forward_mutation`.

4. Coordinator batching framing reconciled. The "batched buffer / flush at session end" wording contradicted write-through and was corrected in `requirements.requirement.coordinator-amortized-flush`, `requirements.requirement.coordinator-buffer-derived-only`, `requirements.requirement.session-mutation-coordinator`, `domain.entity.mutation-session`, `solution.container.mutation-coordinator`, and `solution.component.session-lifecycle`: amortization = one DB open/parse across the session; it never defers visibility. `solution.note.coordinator-planned-anchoring` updated to name write-through-projection.

5. Domain + constraint. Added `domain.entity.graph-reader`, `domain.service.graph-read`, `domain.value.read-visibility` (driven by the new requirements; entity/service realised-by session-routing). Added global law `global.constraint.immediate-queryability` relating it to metadata-mutation-no-rescan, durable-state-authoritative, and db-rebuildable-projection.

6. Note on values. `domain.value.read-visibility` is a value (a measure, like the existing `domain.value.projection-consistency`) and so is deliberately NOT the source of a `realised-by` edge — the binary permits `realised-by` only from group/entity/service. The reader-facing behaviour is realised by `solution.component.session-routing` via `domain.service.graph-read` and `domain.entity.graph-reader`.

7. Plan revisit [required]. The plan's phase-02/03/05 `Satisfies` edges and the buffer tasks must be revisited: `derived-projection-buffer` no longer exists; the coordinator's flush-at-end tasks and the `apg.session.ProjectionBuffer` planned nodes are superseded by synchronous write-through, and the read-through routing work (touching `apg.cmd_query`) is new. No plan mutations were made here (out of scope for the spec-writer).
